examples.en: I'll gratefully accept the gift.
I gratefully ate the lunch box my friend gave me.
I used the umbrella you lent me gratefully and returned it.
I want to spend today gratefully too.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 받은 친절을 감사히 기억할게요.
examples.en: I'll gratefully remember the kindness I received during the trip.
I listened gratefully to the advice my teacher gave me.

explain: '감사히'는 '받다, 먹다, 쓰다' 앞에 붙여서 고마운 마음으로 한다는 느낌을 더해요. 그냥 고마움을 말할 때는 '감사합니다, 고마워요'를 써요. '감사히 잘 먹겠습니다'는 격식 있는 자리에서 많이 해요.

phrases.en: Teacher, thank you, I will enjoy this meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 대접받을 때 격식 있게 하는 인사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal thing to say when someone treats you to food.

phrases.en: I will gratefully use the umbrella you lent me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 물건을 고마운 마음으로 쓰겠다는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say you will use a received item with gratitude.

phrases.en: I'll gratefully accept the gift my friend gave me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감사히'보다 편하게 말할 때 쓰는 비슷한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar but more casual way to say it than 감사히.

explain_en: 감사히 sits before verbs like 받다, 먹다 and 쓰다 to add a grateful feeling. To simply thank someone, say 감사합니다 or 고마워요. '감사히 잘 먹겠습니다' is common at formal meals.

examples.ko: 새로 산 김치냉장고에 김치를 가득 넣었어요.
examples.en: I filled the new kimchi refrigerator with kimchi.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 김치냉장고가 두 대 있어요.
examples.en: My family has two kimchi refrigerators.

examples.ko: 김치냉장고 덕분에 김치를 오래 두고 먹어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the kimchi refrigerator, I can keep kimchi for a long time.
My mother brought some kimchi out of the kimchi refrigerator.
I'm going to put the kimchi refrigerator in the corner of the kitchen.
When we move, shall we take the kimchi refrigerator too?

explain: 일반 냉장고와 따로 두고 쓰는, 김치를 보관하는 전용 냉장고예요. 그래서 '냉장고'와 구별해서 말하고, 물건은 한 대, 두 대로 세요.

phrases.example: 올해 김치냉장고 한 대를 새로 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought a new kimchi refrigerator this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이라서 '한 대, 두 대'처럼 '대'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is counted with 대, like other machines.

phrases.en: Please keep the kimchi in the kimchi refrigerator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치를 보관한다고 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for storing kimchi.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in the kimchi refrigerator

phrases.en: The milk and fruit are in the refrigerator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치냉장고와 구별해서 일반 음식을 보관하는 보통 냉장고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The regular refrigerator for general food, as opposed to the kimchi one.

explain_en: This is a separate refrigerator used only for storing kimchi, so people distinguish it from a regular '냉장고'. You count it with 대: 한 대, 두 대.

examples.en: I'll be in charge of this work from now on.

examples.ko: 다음 학기에는 이 반을 누가 담당하나요?
examples.en: Who will be in charge of this class next semester?
Teacher Kim is in charge of the Korean class.
Last year I was in charge of the new project.
There's a staff member who handles customer inquiries.
If we split the work and each take a part, it's much faster.

explain: 일이나 반, 고객처럼 대상을 책임지고 맡을 때 써요. '맡다'가 더 일상적이고, '담당하다'는 회사나 학교의 역할을 말할 때 많이 나와요. 명사 '담당'은 '담당 선생님', '담당자'처럼 사람 앞뒤에 붙여요.

phrases.en: I will take care of this event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '담당하다'보다 일상적인 말이라서 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than '담당하다', common in conversation.

phrases.example: 우리 반 담당 선생님은 김 선생님이에요.
phrases.en: The teacher in charge of our class is Mr. Kim.
phrases.nuance_ko: '담당'을 사람 앞에 붙여 책임지는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '담당' placed before a person names the one in charge.

phrases.en: Please call the person in charge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 학교에서 그 일을 맡은 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person responsible for a task at a company or school.

explain_en: It is for taking responsibility for a task, class, or customers. '맡다' is more everyday, while '담당하다' shows up for roles at companies and schools. The noun '담당' attaches to people, as in '담당 선생님' and '담당자' (the person in charge).

examples.en: I had a chicken rice bowl for lunch.

examples.ko: 덮밥은 빨리 먹을 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like rice bowls because I can eat them fast.
This restaurant is famous for its beef rice bowl.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 덮밥 위에 반숙 계란을 올려요.
examples.en: I put a soft-boiled egg on top of the warm rice bowl.
Today I tried making a rice bowl myself.

examples.ko: 바쁠 때는 간단하게 덮밥으로 한 끼 해결해요.
examples.en: When I'm busy, I keep it simple and have a rice bowl for a meal.

explain: 덮밥은 '제육덮밥', '연어덮밥'처럼 앞에 올라가는 재료 이름을 붙여서 메뉴를 만들어요. 비빔밥은 먹기 전에 모두 비비지만, 덮밥은 보통 올린 채로 떠먹거나 조금만 섞어요. 혼자 빨리 먹는 한 그릇 식사로 인기가 많아요.

phrases.en: I ordered a salmon rice bowl today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올라가는 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 메뉴를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the topping name in front to name the dish.

phrases.en: One bowl of donburi is enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 덮밥은 '그릇'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rice bowls are counted with 그릇.

phrases.en: I often go to the rice bowl place in front of my office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이름 뒤에 '집'을 붙여 식당을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 집 after a food name to mean a restaurant for it.

explain_en: Menu names are made by putting the topping first, as in '제육덮밥' (spicy pork) and '연어덮밥' (salmon). 비빔밥 is mixed completely before eating, while 덮밥 is usually eaten with the topping on top or mixed only a little. It is popular as a quick one-bowl meal for eating alone.

examples.en: I put cold water in the water bottle.
A water bottle is sitting on the table.

examples.ko: 마시고 남은 물병을 냉장고에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: Please put the water bottle with the leftover water in the fridge.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 새 물병을 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: Before the trip, I bought a new water bottle.
The water bottle is empty, so I need to refill it.

examples.ko: 물병 뚜껑을 꽉 닫지 않으면 가방이 젖어요.
examples.en: If you don't close the water bottle lid tightly, your bag gets wet.

explain: '물병'은 식탁이나 냉장고에 두고 쓰는 병에 가깝고, 운동이나 학교에 들고 다니는 튼튼한 통은 '물통'을 더 많이 써요. 가게에서 사 마시는 물은 '생수'라고 하고, 다 마신 빈 병은 '페트병'이라고 불러요. 물은 '물 한 병'처럼 '병'으로 세어요.

phrases.en: I put the empty water bottle in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빈'은 안에 아무것도 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 빈 means there is nothing inside.

phrases.en: Please put one water bottle in the fridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병은 '하나', '두 개'처럼 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Bottles are counted like 하나, 두 개.

phrases.en: I bought a bottle of water at the convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 사 마시는 물은 '생수'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Bottled water you buy in a store is called 생수.

explain_en: 물병 is closer to a bottle kept on the table or in the fridge, while a sturdy one carried to exercise or school is more often called 물통. Water you buy at a shop is 생수, and the empty plastic bottle afterward is a 페트병. You count water with '병', as in '물 한 병'.

examples.en: The nurse assists the doctor from beside.
The part-timer is assisting the cook.

examples.ko: 시에서 월세를 보조해 줘서 부담이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The city subsidizes my rent, so the burden is smaller.
There is a separate assistant who helps the teacher.

examples.ko: 일을 보조할 사람이 한 명 더 필요해요.
examples.en: We need one more person to help with the work.

examples.ko: 동생이 제 발표를 보조해서 훨씬 쉬웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling helped with my presentation, so it was much easier.

explain: 주로 일하는 사람 옆에서 거들거나, 돈으로 일부를 보태 줄 때 써요. 일상에서는 '돕다'가 더 자연스럽고, 돈을 보태 주는 쪽은 '보조금'이라는 말로도 자주 만나요. 얼굴의 '보조개'는 소리만 비슷한 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: My friend helps me with my work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural word in everyday speech.

phrases.en: My younger sibling assists me with my work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옆에서 거들어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when helping from the side as an assistant.

phrases.en: The government gives a subsidy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈으로 일부를 보태 주는 것을 명사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for money given to cover part of a cost.

explain_en: It is used for assisting the main person at work or for helping out with part of the money. In daily talk '돕다' is more natural, and for money you often meet the word '보조금' (subsidy). '보조개' (dimple) only sounds similar and is a different word.

dis.h: assist in a supporting role; subsidize

p.n: The original is a formal supporting job role; the replacement is general help.

examples.en: I pinned the wet socks up with clothespins.
I didn't have enough clothespins, so I bought more.

examples.ko: 이불을 널 때는 빨래집게를 여러 개 써요.
examples.en: I use several clothespins when hanging out a blanket.
Clothespins are sold cheaply at housewares stores.
One of the clothespins broke.
I hang socks in a row on the clothespins to dry.

explain: '빨래'에 물건을 집는 도구 '집게'가 붙은 말이에요. 빨래는 '널다', '걷다'와 같이 쓰고, 널 때 '빨래집게로 집다'라고 해요. 빨래를 걸어 두는 건조대와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I hang the laundry with clothes pins.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨래집게를 쓰는 대표적인 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical job that uses clothes pins.

phrases.en: I take down the laundry and remove the clothes pins.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마른 빨래를 거둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking down dry laundry.

phrases.en: I pinned it with a clothes pin so it wouldn't blow away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 나타내는 '-로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -로 to show the tool.
phrases.en_equiv: to pin with a clothes pin

explain_en: It combines '빨래' (laundry) with '집게', a gripping tool. Laundry goes with '널다' (hang out) and '걷다' (take in), and you '빨래집게로 집다' to pin it. It is different from a drying rack.

examples.en: I go to the baseball stadium with a friend on weekends.
I watched the game while eating chicken at the baseball stadium.
It is very crowded in front of the baseball stadium.

examples.ko: 우리 집에서 야구장까지 지하철로 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes from my home to the baseball stadium by subway.
The newly built baseball stadium is really big.
At the baseball stadium I sang along loudly to the cheering songs.

explain: '종목 이름 + 장'으로 만들어서 야구장, 축구장, 농구장, 골프장이라고 해요. 야구장은 응원가를 함께 부르고 치킨 같은 간식을 먹으며 보는 분위기로 유명해요. 경기를 하는 곳을 두루 부르는 말은 '경기장'이에요.

phrases.example: 새 경기장이 우리 집 근처에 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A new stadium opened near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 경기를 하는 곳을 두루 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general word for any place where sports games are played.

phrases.en: I go to the baseball stadium on Sunday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구를 보러 갈 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for going to watch baseball.

phrases.en: I cheered loudly at the baseball stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구장은 응원 분위기로 유명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Baseball stadiums are known for their cheering atmosphere.

explain_en: Korean forms these by adding '장' to the sport: 야구장, 축구장, 농구장, 골프장. Baseball parks are known for fans singing cheering songs together and snacking on things like fried chicken. The general word for any sports venue is '경기장'.

examples.en: Payday is the 25th of every month.

examples.ko: 월급날에는 친구들과 맛있는 걸 먹으러 가요.
examples.en: On payday I go out to eat something tasty with friends.
When payday comes, I pay my card bill first.

examples.ko: 이번 월급날에 부모님께 용돈을 드릴 거예요.
examples.en: On this payday I'm going to give my parents some pocket money.

examples.ko: 월급날만 기다리다가 한 달이 다 갔어요.
examples.en: I just waited for payday and the whole month passed.

examples.ko: 월급날 전에는 돈이 없어서 집에서 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: Before payday I have no money, so I eat at home.

explain: '급여일'이라는 말도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 '월급날'이 자연스러워요. '월급이 들어오다'처럼 돈이 통장에 들어오는 표현과 같이 자주 써요. '월급날이다!'처럼 기쁜 기분을 말할 때도 좋아요.

phrases.en: My salary came into my account today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급날에 돈이 통장에 들어오는 걸 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says the pay arrived in your bank account on payday.

phrases.en: Wow, today is payday!
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 마음을 반말로 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, happy exclamation in informal speech.

phrases.en: I have to spend carefully until the next payday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까지'와 함께 다음 월급 때까지의 기간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'kkaji' it marks the time until the next payday.

explain_en: There is also the word '급여일', but in daily talk '월급날' sounds natural. It goes well with phrases like '월급이 들어오다' (the pay comes into your account). You can also say '월급날이다!' to share a happy mood.

examples.en: Mom is setting the dinner table in the kitchen.
All the side dishes on the dinner table are delicious.
I'll help you clear the dinner table.

examples.ko: 저녁상 앞에서 아이들이 숙제 얘기를 했어요.
examples.en: The kids talked about homework at the dinner table.
Dinner is all set, so come on over.
I'll keep tonight's dinner table simple.

explain: '저녁 식사'보다 집에서 차려 놓은 상이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요. '저녁상을 차리다', '저녁상을 물리다(치우다)'처럼 짝으로 써요. 같은 방식으로 '아침상'도 있어요.

phrases.en: I set the dinner table with my mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 상에 준비해 놓을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The set phrase for putting food out on the table.

phrases.en: After clearing the dinner table, we ate fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식사 후에 상을 치울 때 써요. '차리다'의 반대 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for clearing the table after a meal, the opposite of '차리다'.

phrases.en: The whole family sat down at the dinner table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차려진 상 앞에 앉아 먹으려는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pictures people sitting at a table that is already set.
phrases.en_equiv: to sit at the dinner table

explain_en: Compared with '저녁 식사', it feels like you can see the table laid out at home. It pairs with '저녁상을 차리다' (set the table) and '저녁상을 물리다' (clear it). In the same way there is '아침상' for breakfast.

examples.ko: 친할머니는 부산에 사시고 외할머니는 서울에 사세요.
examples.en: My paternal grandmother lives in Busan and my maternal grandmother in Seoul.
My grandmother on my father's side made kimchi herself for me.
Every vacation I go to my paternal grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 저는 친할머니를 많이 닮았다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: People tell me I look a lot like my paternal grandmother.
I was happy to get pocket money from my paternal grandmother.

examples.ko: 명절에는 친할머니 댁에 먼저 인사드리러 가요.
examples.en: On holidays we first go to greet my paternal grandmother.

explain: 아버지의 어머니를 말하고, 어머니의 어머니는 '외할머니'예요. 직접 부를 때는 그냥 '할머니'라고 하고 구분해서 이야기할 때만 '친할머니'라고 해요. 높임은 '친할머니께서', '친할머니께'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: My paternal grandmother went to the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어를 높일 때 '께서'를 붙이고 동사에도 '-시-'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '께서' for the subject and '-시-' on the verb to show respect.

phrases.en: I go to my paternal grandmother's house during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집'의 높임말 '댁'을 써서 할머니 집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '댁' is the honorific for 'house' when speaking of a grandmother's home.

phrases.en: Both of my grandmothers dote on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 할머니를 구분해서 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to distinguish and mention both grandmothers together.

explain_en: It means your father's mother, while your mother's mother is '외할머니'. When addressing her directly you just say '할머니', and use '친할머니' only to distinguish when talking about her. For honorifics, use '친할머니께서' and '친할머니께'.

examples.en: In a soccer match, passes have to be accurate.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 짧은 패스를 아주 잘해요.
examples.en: That player is very good at short passes.

examples.ko: 버스 패스를 사면 한 달 동안 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you buy a bus pass, you can ride for a month.
I'd be satisfied just to pass this exam.

examples.ko: 공원에서 친구와 공으로 패스 연습을 했어요.
examples.en: I practiced passing a ball with a friend in the park.

examples.ko: 입장 패스가 없으면 안으로 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't go inside without an entry pass.

explain: 축구·농구에서 공을 동료에게 주는 것은 '패스를 하다/주다'라고 해요. 버스나 놀이공원에서는 정해진 기간 동안 쓰는 이용권도 패스라고 불러요. 시험에서는 '합격'이 더 흔하고 '패스'는 가볍게 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: That player made a pass to a teammate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공을 동료에게 주는 것을 말하고 '패스하다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Giving the ball to a teammate, same meaning as 'paseu-hada'.

phrases.en: The forward received a good pass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공을 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the player who receives the ball.

phrases.en: I passed this exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에서는 '패스'보다 '합격'이 더 흔하고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For exams, 'hapgyeok' is more common and natural than 'paseu'.

explain_en: In soccer and basketball you 'do' or 'give' a pass. A ticket valid for a set period on a bus or at a theme park is also called a pass. For exams '합격' is more common; 'pass' is the casual version.

dis.h: casual loanword; ball pass or passing a test

p.n: 패스 is casual and also used for a ball pass. 합격 is the standard word for passing a test.

en: to pass (a ball); to skip or pass on something

examples.en: I'll pass on this week's team dinner.
That player passed the ball to a teammate.

examples.ko: 어려운 문제는 일단 패스하고 다음 문제로 가세요.
examples.en: Skip the hard question for now and go on to the next one.
I'm tired today, so I'm skipping the dinner plans.

examples.ko: 이번 시험을 패스하면 다음 단계로 올라가요.
examples.en: If you pass this test, you move up to the next level.

examples.ko: 먼저 패스한 사람은 밖에서 기다려도 돼요.
examples.en: Those who passed first can wait outside.

explain: '이번엔 패스할게요'처럼 하고 싶지 않은 일이나 차례를 가볍게 넘길 때 입말에서 많이 써요. 윗사람에게 정중하게 거절할 때는 '다음에 할게요'나 '참석이 어려워요'가 더 안전해요. 스포츠에서는 '공을 패스하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I skipped lunch today because I was busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '패스하다'보다 덜 가볍고, 순서나 끼니를 빼고 넘어간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less casual than 'paseu-hada', meaning to leave out a turn or a meal.

phrases.en: I'm tired today, so I'll do it next time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있는 정중하고 안전한 거절이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite, safe way to decline, even to someone older.

phrases.en: This question is hard. Can I pass on it?
phrases.nuance_ko: 차례나 문제를 넘기고 싶을 때 가볍게 물어보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to ask if you can skip a turn or question.

explain_en: In casual speech, '이번엔 패스할게요' lightly skips something you don't want to do or a turn. To politely decline to a superior, '다음에 할게요' or '참석이 어려워요' is safer. In sports it is simply passing the ball.
